title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its policy stance on AI. It commits to improving oversight, ensuring transparency, and promoting responsible use of AI within public services.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The document gives a government overview of the EU AI Regulation 2024/1689, which creates harmonised rules for how artificial intelligence can be developed, deployed and used across EU member states. It explains that the regulation amends several existing EU regulations and directives to better address AI risks, protect consumers, and encourage responsible innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining a framework to regulate how artificial intelligence is used in the UK’s qualifications sector, aiming to safeguard the integrity and fairness of exams and assessments. The policy was developed in response to a joint request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, and will set guidelines, oversight mechanisms and compliance standards for AI deployment in certification processes.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This document examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems and evaluates the legal and ethical impacts of those practices. It offers guidance and recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with the advancement of AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It outlines the government’s plans and measures to address the committee’s recommendations and strengthen AI governance, safety, and innovation in the country.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference and frequently asked questions for a committee reviewing artificial intelligence and public standards. It defines the committee’s scope, objectives, and procedural guidelines to guide their assessment of AI’s impact on public standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence. The submission offers the Committee insights into how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explains how artificial intelligence is changing the way medical products are regulated. It details how to apply the principles from the AI White Paper to create fair, safe, and effective regulations.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This policy outlines how the Defence sector plans to use artificial intelligence to become a world‑class force in innovation, efficiency, trust, and influence for its size. It focuses on integrating advanced AI technologies into operations and decision‑making to improve effectiveness and maintain a leading edge in defence capabilities.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan details how the UK Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to unlock the benefits of artificial intelligence while carefully managing its risks. It sets out measures to encourage innovation, improve safety and ensure ethical use of AI across road, rail, and other transport modes.
